nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records (ADR G1)
nodes.description: 4 ADRs backed by Redis 7 spike (INTEGRATION_VERIFIED). ADR-1: Durable publication = transactional outbox + binlog CDC with durable offsets. Rejected DB::afterCommit()-only (process can die after commit). afterCommit() kept as latency hint only. Schema-level idempotency: unique (source, source_event_id) on raw_sensor_events, unique (sensor_reading_id, alert_rule_id) on alerts. ADR-2: Client recovery = lean V1 lifecycle-triggered one-shot authenticated snapshot + resubscribe. No periodic GET. ADR-3: DLQ = dedicated iot.dead-letter-events stream (spike-proven). failed_jobs acceptable for queue relay failures. Batch 100, 5 attempts, bounded backoff. ADR-4: Internal fan-out = direct browser-delivery-v1 consumer → Pusher-compatible broadcaster. No Redis Pub/Sub until horizontal scaling needed.
nodes.rationale: The architecture decisions that bind all implementation stages. ADR-1 is the most critical: it defines the entire publication topology and rejects the simpler afterCommit()-only approach with a concrete justification.
